meta.workDescription: The 406 AEW staff operates primarily within an administrative office environment. Personnel perform command support, legal, historical, public affairs, spiritual, and advisory duties. The physical workspace consists of office suites, cubicles, conference rooms, and standard administrative equipment (computers, copiers, paper shredders). Operations are generally conducted during standard duty hours, with the exception of the Command Post, which operates 24/7.

meta.riskManagementNotes:
Address hazard identification, control selection, local escalation expectations, and when RM refresher training must be completed for this work center.

The Four Principles of RM 
These principles govern when and how to apply the RM process.

Accept No Unnecessary Risk: The Air Force inherently accepts risk to accomplish the mission, but any risk that does not contribute to the objective is unnecessary and must be mitigated or avoided.

Make Risk Decisions at the Appropriate Level: The person making the decision must have the authority, resources, and experience to accept the risk. If a hazard cannot be mitigated at the squadron level, the risk decision must be elevated to the Group or Wing Commander.

Integrate RM into Operations, Activities, and Planning At All Levels: RM is not an after thought or an add-on. It must be built into planning from the very beginning (e.g., assessing electrical capacity beforemoving a new high-powered printer into an office).

Apply the Process Cyclically and Continuously: RM doesn't stop once a plan is executed. You must continuously monitor the situation and adjust mitigations if the environment or mission changes.

The Two Levels of RMHow you apply RM depends on how much time you have.

Deliberate RM: Used when there is ample time for formal planning. It involves thorough research, formal hazard identification, documented risk assessments (like a formal Deliberate Risk AssessmentWorksheet - DRAW), and coordinated approval. (Example: Planning a large-scale CRG deploymentexercise).

Real-Time RM: The mental process applied "on the fly" when time is short or the situation changes rapidly. It relies heavily on experience, training, and situational awareness. (Example: A forklift driverpausing an operation because sudden heavy rain drastically reduces visibility on the flightline).

meta.emergencyEquipment:
Fire Extinguisher Locations:
Personnel can locate extinguishers at every building exit, as well as in specific, designated interior locations. These additional placements include adjacent to the second-floor kitchen, centrally located within the vault hallway, and at the terminus of the corridor near the Chief of Staff's office.

Fire Alarm Pull-Station Locations:
Pll stations are located at every building egress point for immediate use during an evacuation. Furthermore, pull-stations are prominently mounted on the walls along all designated fire escape routes, ensuring personnel can easily activate the alarm while egressing the facility.

selectedModules.title: Ergonomics / Office and Administrative Workstation Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; OSHA ergonomics guidance; local Bioenvironmental Engineering or Occupational Health guidance
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Cover workstation setup, chair adjustment, monitor height and distance, keyboard and mouse position, neutral posture, repetitive motion, micro-pauses or task variation, safe lifting of office supplies, file cabinet and storage safety, early reporting of discomfort, and how to request a BE ergonomic assessment when needed.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA ergonomics guidance; local BE/OEH procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use DAFMAN 91-203 office safety and ergonomics guidance to brief administrative and computer-based workers on musculoskeletal disorder risk factors, workstation adjustment, posture, repetitive motion controls, manual handling of office materials, and supervisor follow-up for ergonomic concerns.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 2

selectedModules.title: Fetal Protection Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 48-146 - Occupational Health Program Management; AFRCI 41-104 - Professional Board and National Certification Examinations as applicable
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use AF occupational and public health guidance to brief reproductive hazards, reporting expectations, and referral procedures. No direct OSHA 2254 module is mapped here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DAFMAN 48-146 - Occupational Health Program Management / local procedures

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: Common local training item often broken out separately with fixed and portable ladder rules
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use local ladder lesson plans, manufacturer instructions, and AF walking-working surface guidance. OSHA 2254 (2015 edition) does not provide a dedicated general-industry ladder training summary in the same way it does for lockout, forklifts, or confined spaces, so this remains primarily AF/local-driven.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Personnel using ladders at any working height must be trained when first assigned, and that training must include hands-on instruction covering ladder defects, electrocution hazards, positioning, and placement for various job sites. Training must be documented under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 7.4.3.7
